data.body:
Root cause: `_promote` persisted `PR_CREATED` after promotion, then returned when `await_pr_close` was false. `count_active_runs` and `active_workflow` treat `PR_CREATED` as active, so a completed workflow held a concurrency slot until orphan reconciliation changed it to `CANCELLED`.

Phase 1 evidence: an instrumented no-wait workflow returned `pr_promoted` with persisted states ending in `PR_CREATED`. `test_active_query_selects_state` showed `PR_CREATED` remains active.

Working example: an await-close workflow persisted `AWAITING_PR_CLOSE`, waited for `submit_pr_closed`, then persisted `COMPLETED` after merge.

Hypothesis confirmed: persisting `COMPLETED` only on the no-wait path matches the workflow outcome and releases the active slot.

Hypothesis refuted: the pull request close resolver must keep no-wait rows signalable. Evidence showed the no-wait workflow has already returned. Resolver tests prove terminal rows are ignored while `AWAITING_PR_CLOSE` rows remain preferred.

Falsification check: after the fix was green, I removed the production `await persist(COMPLETED)` line. `pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k no_wait_promotion_persists_completed_terminal_state` failed with final states `['PR_CREATED', 'PR_CREATED']`. I restored the fix and the selector passed.

Plan review: PASS with 0 blocking and 0 advisory findings.

Acceptance selectors: `pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k no_wait_promotion_persists_completed_terminal_state` passed. `pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pr_close_workflow.py -k await_pr_close_path_persists_awaiting_pr_close` passed. `pytest tests/unit/test_pr_events.py -k resolver_ignores_terminal_execution_rows` passed. `pytest tests/unit/test_pr_events.py -k resolver_prioritizes_awaiting_pr_close_workflow` passed. `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py -k active_count_excludes_completed_executions` passed.

CI: `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` passed with ruff clean, 1462 passed, 6 skipped, and `[eval-gate] PASS`.

Bug class: preexisting. The no-wait promotion path lacked a terminal persist call in the shipped workflow rather than failing because of environment integration or test flakiness.
